column3: Description
Full‑screen cards users swipe left/right Tinder‑style—commonly used for onboarding tips.
Sidebar shows step checklist; main area swaps content per step—great for sign‑ups.
Preset color palette and enlarged hit‑areas optimized for low‑vision users.
List items set inside a soft card, giving a grouped feel.
Full‑width monospaced table that autoscrolls new rows into view for real‑time logs.
List items gain visible focus rings and arrow‑key traversal without a mouse.
Main sidebar plus a collapsible sub‑sidebar for deep navigation hierarchies.
Primary column anchored to the right edge, leaving whitespace on the left for asymmetry.
Multiple slide‑in drawers that can stack without covering each other—useful for nested forms.
Hides headers/footers and centers content in a 16:9 frame for on‑screen demos.
Allows users to drag items up or down to change their order.
A row containing twelve equal grid units so items can span custom widths.
Sidebar stays in view while the main content scrolls independently.
Sequence of items automatically numbered for steps or rankings.
Horizontal list of cards that scrolls with arrow buttons or swipes.
Each list item separated by subtle borders for clear visual breaks.
Vertical list with dots and connecting line to display events chronologically.
Overlapping cards that users swipe or click through, deck‑style.
Items sorted under sticky A‑Z headings, useful for contact directories.
Masonry grid that fetches and appends new items only when they enter viewport.
List items highlight and raise slightly on hover to indicate clickability.
A fixed‑width wrapper that keeps content centered with equal margins on large screens.
Header remains visible at the top even as users scroll down long pages.
Left pane shows a list; selecting an item fills the right pane with details.
Squares keep their aspect ratio regardless of screen width—great for photo grids.
Narrow rail on the right where threaded comments stay visible while the main document scrolls.
Classic fixed header, fixed footer, flexible middle flanked by two sidebars.
Sidebar groups nav links into collapsible accordion sections.
Hierarchical list where nodes expand to reveal child items.
Sidebar turns into a top tab bar on small screens to save horizontal space.
Vertical list with optional badges or icons for each item.
Horizontal track of small cards with snap points—good for related products.
Sections piled vertically with generous spacing, creating a scroll‑friendly flow.
Responsive two‑column (tablet) to three‑column (desktop) layout for editorial articles.
Clicking an item reveals hidden details beneath it—like an inline accordion.
Combines table rows with richer list‑style content, like avatars and buttons.
Square icons in a grid acting as quick‑launch shortcuts.
Renders only items in view, keeping long lists smooth and memory‑light.
A simple side‑by‑side layout that splits the screen into equal halves.
Table rows reduced in height for displaying large datasets in admin panels.
Alternating background colors improve readability for long item lists.
Tiles of varying heights that pack tightly without gaps—ideal for image galleries.
Vertical timeline down the left with horizontal bars depicting durations per row.
Mobile‑first full‑height cards that swipe vertically (TikTok/YouTube Shorts style).
Equal‑height cards arranged in responsive rows for product or blog previews.
A narrow navigation column on the left with a wider content pane on the right.
Two‑line items with avatar, subject, and timestamp—suitable for messages.
Two stacked header rows—primary category plus secondary labels—for complex data.
List of audio or video tracks with play buttons and duration labels.
A 4‑ or 6‑cell masonry grid sized for KPI cards and charts—ideal for analytics home screens.
Keeps footer docked to the bottom of the viewport when content is short.
Horizontally scrollable columns holding draggable cards for task workflows.
Left list of conversations, right pane for active chat with sticky message input.
Flexbox row ensuring each child fills the tallest sibling’s height.
Series of panels shown one at a time with “Next” and “Back” controls.
Divides content into three equal vertical columns, perfect for feature overviews.
Overlapping sections with intentional z‑index stacking to create depth (hero over nav, etc.).
Replaces standard bullets with custom icons for stronger visual cues.
Bottom‑fixed action bar (save, share) that appears once the user scrolls past hero.
Three short columns meant for sidebar widgets rather than full boards.
First column (e.g., names) stays fixed while remaining list area scrolls horizontally.
Universal wrapper housing header, sidebar, and content slot for SPA routing.
Automatically loads more items as the user nears the bottom.
Content on the left, slim sidebar on the right—great for ads or related links.

Square thumbnails with titles underneath, common in video libraries.
Thumbnail rail at top; clicking loads large media preview and metadata below.
A responsive grid of four equal blocks that collapse gracefully on small screens.
Each list item includes a checkbox for task completion tracking.
Sidebar hidden off‑canvas that slides in from the edge on button click.
Persistent header bar with the page content scrolling beneath it.
Large overlay displaying a scrollable list while the background remains visible.
Two resizable panes side‑by‑side (code ↔ preview or markdown ↔ render) with a draggable divider.
Centered, narrow input overlay that appears above a dimmed app shell for quick command search.
Left half for media, right half for text—often used on landing pages.
Stretches edge‑to‑edge, resizing smoothly across any viewport.
Tiles include small corner badges for statuses like “New” or numbers.
Breaks large sets into pages with numbered navigation links.

Small thumbnail on the left with text stacking on the right—used for comment lists.
